messages.subject: CORS and Shiny?
parts:
Shiny is ... I hate to say this ... fantastic!  (I hate R, but I gotta give the devil his/her due ...)

Anyway, I'd like to be able to "embed" shiny in another web app (pylons/pyramid-based) but NOT as an IFRAME element.  Rather, I'd
like to be able to use a jQuery "load" into a <DIV> or other container.   Consequently, I need to use Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
which means I need to be able to add a header to the server responses.  I've tried searching these forii and can't find anything regarding how to access
or modify shiny response other than vague (and, apparently incorrect) references to resp$headers or response$headers.

Help is, of course, appreciated.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Re: CORS and Shiny?
parts:
Not at all.  But, when I went to that link, I immediately got a page with an angry pink unicorn on it saying "this page is taking too long to load."

I'm guessing the server is out getting shave and a haircut somewhere and will be back sometime after morning tea?

In the alternative, what I'd submit would be something along the lines of ...

There is currently no apparent (or documented) way to access (or construct) the response object.    This would be useful in being able to add, remove, or modify
http headers, for instance.    Although most such headers can be added by using the <meta http-equiv="..." > tag, there is at least one exception, which requires,
for security reasons, that the header be added by the server proper:  Access-Control-Accept-Origin.  This is part of the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (W3C) standard
which allows controlled accesses to multiple different servers from within the same web page.   One can do this using IFRAMEs but because these are completely isolated
from their peer DOM objects those peers cannot access the IFRAME's contents.  Hence, no resources can be shared this way.  By allowing cross-origin access, 
a DIV or other, non-isolating container can be loaded (via  jQuery's load method, for instance) from a site other than the one the page itself came from.

Example:

I have a website at http://localhost:8080/index.html looking something like:

<html>
<head>
...
<script type="javascript">
$(function() {
   $("shiny-div").load("http://localhost:8100/", function() { initShiny() });
});
</script>
</head>
<body>
<h1> This is an example of embedding shiny ala CORS</h1>
<div id="shiny-div"></div>
</body>
</html>

(I've left out or oversimplified a bunch of stuff, but it gives yout he general idea.)

On the shiny (server) side I'll get a collection of headers that include:

    Origin:  http://localhost:8080

So my shiny server will have to put a header in the response that looks like:

   Access-Control-Accept-Origin: http://localhost:8080

to allow cross-site access specifically from localhost:8080, or

   Access-Control-Accept-Origin: *

to allow cross-site access from any host.    WARNING:  this can leave you vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, so BEWARE!
